title: Who owed what to whom?
question: How did holding land turn into a web of obligations in medieval Europe?
hook: Without a way to pay its horsemen, an empire found another way to reward them.
idea: Feudalism tied land to service, and it often began when an empire could not support its cavalry any other way.

beats.prompt: An empire in the 9th century has cavalry but lacks the bureaucracy needed to support it. What does it do?

choices.label: It allocates land to its mounted troops
It sends the cavalry home
choices.feedback: This is tempting, but the empire still had mounted troops to support.

choices.label: It builds a larger bureaucracy first
choices.feedback: This is tempting, but the empire lacked that infrastructure, which is why it gave out land.

beats.explain: Lacking the bureaucratic infrastructure to support cavalry, the Carolingian Empire gave land to its mounted troops.

beats.prompt: Match each name to what it is tied to.
pairs: Obligations of the warrior nobility: lords, vassals and fiefs
Obligations of the nobility, the clergy and the peasantry
First introduced the word feudalism, in 1771
beats.explain: Ganshof's definition is narrow, Bloch's covers all three estates, and Whitaker introduced the word feudalism.

beats.prompt: Put these in the order they first appeared.
items: Feudālis in a charter of Charles the Fat
The word feudalism from John Whitaker
beats.explain: The charter dates to 884, feudum replacing beneficium to 984, féodal to 1614, and feudalism to 1771.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: The word feudalism is derived from the Latin word feodum, or feudum, meaning fief.
Feodum was a word used during the medieval period.
So people in the Middle Ages must have seen feudalism as a formal political system.
So they would have described their own society with that name.
beats.explain: Although the word comes from a medieval term, the people of the Middle Ages did not conceive of feudalism as a formal political system.
